newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - July 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - July 8.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Tuesday:
* At least four bidders came forward Monday to meet a deadline to bid for Barney's Inc.
* Some Japanese women fear the price of equality will be schedules as arduous as those of Japan's notoriously overworked men.
* British Airways announced plans for a 72-hour strike starting Wednesday.
* Burma-shave is being reintroduced by American Safety Razor Co.
* Both the Dow and the S&P 500 fell Monday.
* Integrated Health Services agreed to buy Rotech Medical.
* Aluminum Co of America said second quarter profits rose 57 percent.
* The Justice Department approved British Telecommunications' takeover of MCI Communications.
* The war over telephone deregulation entered a new realm with a controversy over a newspaper advertisement claiming Nynex has high local phone rates.
* British merchant bank Wertheim Schroder & Co decided to drop the Wertheim name.
* Gold futures prices plunged for a second day.
* The dollar fell to a nearly four-week low against the yen.
